plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by the ascending clock exit points. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it neither costs you when you'd lose anyway (bidding higher just risks overpaying) nor forgoes profitable wins (bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities). Since my value is $31, I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure mirrors a second-price (Vickrey) auction: I exit when the clock reaches my sealed bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own. Bidding my true value ($37) is the dominant strategy here—it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, and I never pay more than the second-highest bid, which is always ≤ my value in a winning scenario. Overbidding risks paying more than the prize is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable auctions.

This auction mechanism effectively functions as a second-price auction: I exit at my sealed bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid. Since my payment doesn't depend on my own bid (only on whether I win and what others bid), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $11.
